context:
You picked b (finish both checks first) and offered your computer, 12:45 CDT. Answer: Recorded b; nothing more to pick. The cloud check runs in lane c203-builder-window. For the local check: in the Claude desktop app, Settings, Claude Code, Remote Control, add your claude-settings checkout folder, then tell me in chat.

You answered none twice: you are open to the per-tier setup (A) but said it needs testing, especially for local sessions, which have no per-session environments but do have agent roles.

What is true today (read Oct 28 from the repo): one value, 500000, for every model, set in settings.json (autoCompactWindow, line 433 on main). A per-model value exists as a form (modelSettings.<model>.autoCompactWindow, which /autocompact writes) but the repo sets none. No agent file in the repo sets its own value.

Measured since by the c203 lane (cloud, Claude Code 2.1.312, Oct 28 19:45 CDT):
- The variable raises the window as well as lowering it: 1000000 gives an effective window of 980000, and 400000 gives 380000. So a coordinator environment can have 1M and a lane environment 400k.
- A helper agent's own autoCompactWindow works as a ceiling: its effective window is the smaller of the session's window (the variable counts) and its own value. So a builder at 300000 in a 400000 lane gets 300000. This was read from the program's own code; a live agent test returned no reading, so it is not yet seen working.

Still untested: a local session (no environments there; each launch can set its own window with the --autocompact flag, or a --settings value, per the docs), because the lane has no local machine.

So most of your testing question is answered; two checks remain.

options.gain: Your tiers take effect in the cloud now, on measured numbers; the two gaps are small and named.
options.how:
Coordinator environment 1000000, lane environment 400000, builder agent file 300000 go in now. A lane then reads a live builder's window in the cloud, and someone on your own computer tests a local launch with its own window flag.
Before: one 500000 value. After: three values, the cloud ones measured; local and a live agent reading checked next.
options.label: Set the numbers per tier now, then check the two leftovers
options.lose: Local sessions keep 500000 until the launch test; a builder's ceiling is read from code, not yet seen live; /autocompact stays unusable where the variable is set.

options.gain: Nothing changes until every piece is seen working, local sessions included.
options.how:
A lane reads a live builder's window, and a local launch is tested on your computer. Only then do the numbers go in.
Before: one 500000 value, nothing changed. After: a fully measured table, then the numbers.
options.label: Finish the two checks first, then set the numbers
options.lose: The limits wait on a local test that needs your computer; the cloud numbers that already work sit unused.

options.gain: /autocompact keeps working on your own computer.
options.how:
The install scripts write ~/.claude/settings.json as a generated copy that carries over only your saved window setting, so /autocompact works and never dirties claude-settings.
Before: /autocompact edits the tracked file through the link. After: it edits a copy.
options.label: Make settings.json a copy made at install, keeping your window
options.lose: Departs from two of your rulings (the link, and the backup rule); other tool writes to the file are lost at each merge; install code to write and test on Mac and Windows; it does not give per-tier limits by itself.

ref: c203 (the compact window is set outside the tracked settings file), lane session_013NEJL4Ghu7Kthvr3kBsiVR; your item 53 a and 58
title: Can each kind of session get its own context limit, and how do we set it?
why: The cloud numbers are measured and your tiers are what you asked for; the two leftovers are small and can be checked after, with local sessions simply staying at 500000 until then.
